description: Parameters needed to the corresponding task specification in eTaSL

from-force_control_task_lib-version-1.0..description:
Library force_control_task_lib version 1.0.3.
 Set to true to indicate that task specification comes from the library above. 
 Library description: Library with eTaSL task specifications for force control tasks for Crospi
Authors: Santiago Iregui (KU Leuven), Erwin Aertbeliën (KU Leuven), Federico Ulloa (KU Leuven)

file_path.description: File path of the corresponding task specification

parameters.description: List of parameters needed to define an instance of the task specification

FT_sensor_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) of the force/torque sensor. The measured wrench of the input channel (wrench_input_channel) is expressed in this frame, with its origin as reference point

weight_tracking.description: Weight [-] of the constraint that rotates the task frame towards the measured contact force (tracking of the contour normal), relative to the other constraints of the same priority

tool_COG.description: Position [m] of the center of gravity of the tool (everything mounted after the force/torque sensor), as [x,y,z] expressed in FT_sensor_frame. Used for the gravity compensation together with tool_weight

task_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) that is controlled, e.g. the tool center point. The contact frame is defined w.r.t. this frame by tf_2_contact_frame

K_force.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the normal force control (inverse of its time constant). Higher values correct force errors faster, but too high values cause oscillations or loss of contact

tf_2_contact_frame.description: Pose of the contact frame w.r.t. task_frame, as [x,y,z,qx,qy,qz,qw] (position in m, unit quaternion with the real part qw last), expressed in task_frame. The origin should be at the contact point (e.g. on the axis of a cylindrical tool at the height of the contour) and the z-axis must be perpendicular to the plane of the contour (e.g. along the axis of a cylindrical tool). The default is the identity (contact frame = task_frame)

filter_cutoff_frequency.description: Cut-off frequency [Hz] of the Butterworth low-pass filter applied to each component of the measured wrench. 0 disables the filter. Lower values give a smoother but more delayed force signal. Keep it well below the Nyquist frequency of the controller (e.g. <= 10 Hz at 100 Hz)

tool_weight.description: Weight [N] (gravity force, not mass) of the tool mounted after the force/torque sensor. Its wrench (gravity along -z of the robot base frame, applied at tool_COG) is subtracted from the measured wrench. 0 disables the gravity compensation (e.g. when the sensor is tared or the simulator does not measure the tool weight)

wrench_input_channel.description: Name of the input channel (type wrench) from which the measured wrench of the force/torque sensor is read: the varname of the input handler that provides it (e.g. a WrenchInputHandler), or the channel fed directly by the robot driver/simulator (name_expr_cartesian_wrench of the MuJoCo simulator). Change it to use another sensor or input handler

tangential_velocity.description: Desired velocity [m/s] of the contact frame along the tangent of the contour (y-axis of the task frame, i.e. the z-axis of the contact frame crossed with the contour normal pointing towards the robot). The sign selects the direction of motion along the contour

filter_order.description: Order of the Butterworth low-pass filter (2, 3 or 4). A higher order attenuates high frequencies more, but adds more delay

weight_hold.description: Weight [-] of the constraints that keep the initial position along the z-axis of the contact frame and the initial orientation of the tool, relative to the other constraints of the same priority. Only matters when the constraints conflict

weight_tangential_velocity.description: Weight [-] of the tangential velocity constraint (y-axis of the task frame) relative to the other constraints of the same priority. Only matters when the constraints conflict

path_length.description: Distance [m] travelled by the origin of the contact frame (integral of its speed, in any direction) after which the task finishes

weight_normal_force.description: Weight [-] of the normal force control constraint (x-axis of the task frame) relative to the other constraints of the same priority. Only matters when the constraints conflict

wrench_convention.description: Sign convention of the wrench received on the input channel (wrench_input_channel). exerted_on_environment: it is the wrench that the robot exerts on the environment (e.g. the MuJoCo simulator); it is negated to obtain the wrench acting on the robot. exerted_on_robot: it is the wrench that the environment exerts on the robot and is used as is. All forces in this task (normal_force, outputs) are forces acting on the robot

normal_force.description: Desired contact force [N] normal to the contour, i.e. the force with which the robot pushes against the contour. It is controlled along the x-axis of the task frame (normal of the contour) as the force that the contour exerts on the robot

K_tracking.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the rotation of the task frame around the z-axis of the contact frame: its angular velocity [rad/s] is K_tracking times the angle [rad] between the x-axis of the task frame and the measured contact force. Higher values track sharper curvatures, but are more sensitive to force noise

K_hold.description: Feedback gain [1/s] to keep the initial position along the z-axis of the contact frame and the initial orientation of the tool. Higher values correct deviations faster

ramp_up_time.description: Time [s] to linearly increase the tangential velocity from zero to tangential_velocity at the start of the task, so that the task frame can first align with the contour. 0 means no ramp (full velocity from the start)

contact_stiffness.description: Estimated stiffness [N/m] of the contact (environment + robot + tool) in the normal direction, used as model of the force control: the velocity towards the contour is K_force*(normal_force - measured normal force)/contact_stiffness. A lower value gives faster but possibly oscillating force control, a higher value slower force control

is-2D_contour_following.description:
Task Specification: 2D_contour_following.etasl.lua
Set to true to indicate that the task uses the task specification mentioned above. 
 Task description: 2D contour following with the task frame formalism. The robot must already be in contact with the contour when the task starts (e.g. after a guarded motion); the contour lies in a plane perpendicular to the z-axis of the contact frame (task_frame*tf_2_contact_frame). A task frame with its origin at the contact frame rotates around that z-axis so that its x-axis follows the measured contact force (the normal of the contour, pointing from the contour towards the robot) and its y-axis is tangent to the contour. In this task frame the robot controls the normal contact force to normal_force (x), moves with tangential_velocity along the contour (y, ramped up during ramp_up_time), and keeps its initial position along z and its initial orientation (only the task frame rotates, which suits rotationally symmetric tools). The measured wrench is read from the input channel named by wrench_input_channel (default "wrench_input") (type wrench, expressed in FT_sensor_frame with its origin as reference point), provided by the robot driver/simulator (e.g. MuJoCo) or by a WrenchInputHandler; it is low-pass filtered, converted to the wrench acting on the robot (see wrench_convention) and compensated for the tool weight. The task finishes (monitor action "exit") when the origin of the contact frame has travelled path_length. Outputs: pose of the contact frame (x_tf, y_tf, z_tf, roll_tf, pitch_tf, yaw_tf), external force on the robot in the task frame and torque in the contact frame (x_force ... z_torque), normal_force, tangential_force, normal_angle, travelled_distance and tangential_speed.
